Stellenbosch under siege?

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
James Hayes is a successful businessman living in Stellenbosch. He grew up there, studied at the university and sees it as his home, but when he moved back there a few years ago he was horrified by the high level of crime and the municipalities apathetic approach towards protecting its residents. He could have sat back like most of us and just paid his subscriptions and attended the local ratepayers meetings. But as a former police reservist he is well versed with the law and how criminals operate. He recognizes the local police are over stretched and security companies have guards that are under paid and poorly trained. Angered by how tourists were being targeted by ATM gangs and the lack of effective policing James took it upon himself to drive them out of town by chasing them and driving into them. He was also angry by the lack of action against the gangs preying on hikers and students in the green belt so he put up a drone, tracked them down, and chased them with the help of local security company and caught 6 or the 7 heavily armed gang. James dedication and unconventional methods ruffle feathers. Nobody likes to be challenged by a private individual who is putting his body on the line to stop crime. He works closely with all the security networks and police and provides them with information from his well established network of informers. He is so disruptive to the gangs trade that they are trying to buy them off, or kill him.

Summary:
Stellenbosch - the iconic university town with its oak-lined streets, cafes, boutiques and art galleries makes it a major tourist destination in the Western Cape. It’s surrounded by prestigious wine farms and home to some of the wealthiest people in the country, but on the outskirts are some of the poorest of the poor, in suburbs like Kayamandi and Cloetesville. The residents of Stellenbosch feel they are under siege, it has the 11th highest crime rate in the country, despite the relatively small population of 180 000 and over seven different security companies operating in town.
It’s a story about how one small town, a microcosm of South Africa, is fighting back with private citizens challenging local municipalities to step up and protect them.

Further information:
There are three levels of crime in Stellenbosch: in the wealthy suburbs it ranges from the usual house break-ins to violent house invasions. In town, the biggest crime is by ATM gangs which move into Stellenbosch from Khayelitsha, Guguletu and Sea Point. With eight ATM syndicates operating in the Western Cape, Stellenbosch makes for easy pickings with plenty of access routes in and out of town. The ATM gangs descend on Stellenbosch in several hired cars, using local car guards to call them when the tourists are in town, and ensure bank security is paid off.
They only target tourists because they don’t have limits on their cards, have insurance and won’t bother to press charges because they won’t be around to appear in court. One morning they made off with R86 000 from just one card holder – they can make millions of rand every month. Once a card is snatched/swopped they pass it so rapidly from one person to the next that the police have given up trying to catch them.
Then there are the students, who account for 1/3rd of crime victims in Stellenbosch. It’s an open campus and students drink in town and fall foul to petty crimes like cell-phones and laptops being snatched, to more extreme crime like kidnapping , rape and murder. First year student Hanna Cornelius was abducted, raped and murdered last April, attacked while sitting talking to a friend in her car in the early hours of the morning.
The farms surrounding Stellenbosch are constantly under attack, the latest victim Jeffrey Zetler, a high profile member of the Stellenbosch community, well loved and respected by his workers. He was murdered in front of his staff on 23rd June as he was locking up. Zetler paid his staff in cash, a fact well known by local criminal networks. He had survived three previous robberies. The head of the Farmers’ Association, Piet Carinus, says most farmers don’t deal in cash anymore because they are followed home from the bank and have given up on expecting protection or help from SAPS.
And then there is Cloetesville and Kayamandi which are ravaged by drugs and gang turf wars. Neighbourhood watch chair Eugene Gordon says that 47 people lost their lives last year in Cloetesville alone.
James Hayes, a successful businessman who grew up in Stellenbosch, studied at the University and recently moved back with his family, was horrified by the high crime rate. Soon after he bought his home he discovered the previous owner was attacked by the infamous crowbar gang on several occasions, and in the last incident he had a gun held to his head. James immediately installed massive lights on top of his home and security cameras on his street. Having been a police reservist for many years, James decided to get actively involved in defending himself and his neighbourhood and made it his business to get to know all the security networks in town. Currently he is the Vice Chair of the Community Policing forum.
James makes for an unusual resident. He spends most of his spare time tracking criminals, regularly patrolling the streets at night. He is on a radio network with several neighbourhood watches, security companies, and has a network of informers. He makes it his business to go out and confront crime as it’s happening. He prides himself in having a bullet proof vest and when his network of informers tells him the ATM gangs are in town he races off after them. The police have given up chasing them, so James has made it his mission - on several occasions when chasing the ATM gangs he has bashed into them using the bullbar on his Nissan, literally driving them out of town, to the extent that the ATM gangs are now scared of him and leave town if they are alerted to his presence.
And like all other people that obstruct their business, the gangs are now offering him R40 000 a month to stay away. That’s not working, so now there are death threats directed at him and his network of informers. But his unconventional methods are having an impact, and ATM crime is right down from where it was over the festive season.
James was tired of the attacks on hikers and runners at African Valley. When he approached the Municipality they refused to put up a sign warning people of gangs in the area saying it was bad for tourism. So James set up a sting. He put a drone up and was directed by radio to where the gang was spotted and chased them down with two local security bringing down 6 of the 7 criminals. He has the drone footage the pictures gang and the weapons. When he catches criminals he profiles them and shares the information with the police and security networks.
James acknowledges that like all South African towns there are just not enough or sufficiently well-trained police officers. They are fighting heavily armed gangs, petty criminals, drug protection syndicates, and civilian protests for better service delivery. The Municipality doesn’t see fighting crime as its responsibility apart from protecting municipal property.
Winelands Security Watch is a new initiative which is sponsored by several wealthy business people who took on the services of security company TSU. They are well-armed and are making an impact in the central zone of Stellenbosch. They have also installed a Licence Plate Recognition system and have begun profiling every ATM criminal, and crime figures are down over the last few months. But all this does is displace crime from well-defended suburbs to areas where the guards are underpaid and poorly trained, making them open to being paid off.
We will go on patrol with the neighbourhood watch in Cloetsville- they have been on the beat for 11 years. With James his daily night patrols and TSU the new crack team in town and see the Licence plate tracking unit. We will also feature the students as they party it up and hear their side of the story. Interview the farmers and Zetlers widow. I already have an interview with one of the ATM gangs who tells us how its done.

Press Release:


Stellenbosch Under Siege
Amid a sustained crime wave engulfing the university and tourist town of Stellenbosch, which culminated in the brutal murder of a strawberry farmer. One local businessman decided to push back and has rallied fellow residents to reclaim ground lost to criminals. Carte Blanche examines the success of his unconventional methods which have ruffled local authorities’ feathers.


Script:


Script: Friday night. Party time on the streets of Stellenbosch in the Western Cape. But instead of hitting the town, businessman James Hayes is out chasing down criminals and giving local police backup because there just aren’t enough of them. Hayes is fed up with the murder and crime that plague this small town.

James “Crime is bad in Stellenbosch is rated 9 in SA with regards to 17 of the community related crimes so it’s bad

01 17 33 18 I live right there, behind those tress. And often I heard about people being attacked here in one week it was 6 separate incidents. I decided to come and make a difference here
Script: James can be seen running through the trees, chasing down seven armed muggers with the help of local law enforcement. They managed to catch 6 of them. He’s not exactly your conventional businessman.
Script: He’s a successful software developer who grew up and studied in Stellenbosch, and returned two years ago
James Crime is bad
Script: On the surface Stellenbosch seems idyllic, with its oak lined streets and rich history, it’s one of South Africa’s top tourist destinations, but there is an underbelly of crime here, that keeps hitting this town. The latest high profile murder shocked the community
Link: 10 minutes from the heart of Stellenbosch is the Zetler strawberry farm, a very well-known land mark for anyone that has visited the area. Tragically Jeffrey Zetler was stabbed to death in a botched robbery at his farm gate.
Script: Six guys jumped Zetler as he opened the gate, stabbing him and then they dragged him to the office door, explains Zetler’s older brother Dennis
Dennis “the alarm went off and then they punched him with a sharp object another 2 or 3 times because he had like 6 holes in his body before he left here so nobody could survive with all that bleeding
Script: He collapsed before he could open the safe and they got away with nothing, says farm manager Jaco Vermeulen
Jaco 07 40 18 14 We don’t know what to say we are speechless 07 39 50 18 it was a quiet Saturday afternoon and this was well planned …people watching our businesses’
Dennis 07 33 11 04 and you just think who is the next one that’s how I fear the whole time
Script: Tourists love the relaxed atmosphere of this student town, filled with art galleries and boutiques, and that’s a magnet for ATM criminals. But they are difficult to catch and prosecute, because they make speedy getaways onto the Cape Flats
Script: As the vice chair of the community policing forum, James has made it his business to bust the ATM gangs after hearing from guest house owner Annemien Kotze how often her clients were victims
Annemein: 07 08 19 07 the guest were very upset when they arrived here it happened about once or twice a week and they just feel it spoiled their whole experience of the town and of Stellenbosch and their holiday to SA
James driving 00 48 17 10 what you have is you will have your spotters standing somewhere in the street alerting the ATM robbers that there are tourists around and not a lot of policemen around
Script: This is one of James’s informants. He has been working with the ATM gangs for the last 10 years.
Eitenne” 11 06 48 17 I must listen to the accent of people talking… you must tell them hoe gaan dit and now you must listen to what they say back to you and if they say dit gan goed or goeden dagen then ..then I know what to do
Link: 01 09 24 05 so underneath this car over here there is a square disk and this is a parking meter which is linked to the town’s system. What they will then do with an unsuspecting tourist is tell them that they need to pay for this parking meter at this ABSA ATM so when the tourist goes there this is where the charm and scam then kicks in
ATM spotter 10 54 29 21 when you put your card inside the machine makes a click sound and the guy always has money in his right hand when the machine makes a click. He slides the card underneath the money and then he has this guy’s card in his hand now and now he tell the guy ok put in your pin 10 55 44 00 any way you move your hand he knows exactly which number you press… he tells you please you must wait the transaction is still in progress and while you wait he goes and he has your card already and he goes to the other machines and draw your money. R83 000 on one card and that is one card and sometimes they are standing there the whole day
Script: The ATM gangs move swiftly, passing the stolen card between them so they’re almost impossible to catch. James had had enough, and was hell-bent on driving them out of town
James 00 27 47 15 so what I started doing was I started following them and I started to disrupt them
Mac “How? how did you disrupt them? That’s quite brave laugh
James” you can take photos of them they don’t like that you can pull them over SAPS will come and they will profile them and search the car
Script: Sometimes when he gives chase in his car they have an accident, or if they’re getting away, he uses his car as a battering ram
James” I had a clear sight to see that there aren’t people around ….. and I just gave gas and I hit them
ATM guy 11 04 07 11 for them he is like a demon to them because when they see him they run away …….when James see the cars and they don’t want to stop then he hit the cars when he is chasing them that’s what James do so they are very scared of James.
Script: ATM crime is down dramatically.
But the other major magnet for crime in this town are the 30 000 university students.
Link: 05 57 05 21 So this is party central in Stellenbosch the students have come out to play the streets are lit and they having an amazing time but this is when they are most vulnerable because they have been drinking they are beyond caring
TSU Doron Cozons 05 43 20 04 you have predators out there you have lots of people coming from different parts of Cape Town they see the naivety of these students. There are syndicates operating around here stealing lots of stuff from students
Script: Last year, the abduction, rape and murder of student Hanna Cornelius, right in town, left the community reeling, but students still take chances despite the massive awareness campaigns. Emma Wieham says students are constantly preyed upon
Emma 03 17 48 06. I know of a girl ...she was walking down Victoria which is the main road of campus, and they opened the car door and they grabbed her cellphone and she didn’t want to let go and they dragged her next to the car down the road. In that area there are a lot of cameras and people still have the audacity to try and get away with something like this
Links 03 59 20 06 The unique thing about Stellenbosch University is that it is right in the heart of town and completely open to the public. The problem here is that anyone can walk right in and for students they become particularly vulnerable for criminals as their laptops their cellphones make for easy pickings
Student 03 02 06 13 I was going to meet someone outside the res …not even two metres from the door he just started running at me. We still don’t know what his intensions were. He didn’t say anything he didn’t ask me for my phone. It was only afterwards that I realised I had been stabbed. It was on my left hand side close to my heart 10 cm deep and it eventually led to my lung collapsing and 4 days in ICU
Script: Professor Stan du Plessis says that after this incident, The university improved the lighting and placed permanent guards at residences
Prof Stan “It is never possible to say the precise reason crime is down is it because of our awareness campaign or of the technology that we use but we can say we have dramatically improved our system and we are happy to report the incidents of crime has declined
Script: But across town in Cloetesville, they have other problems, drugs and gangs, and they don’t have the luxury of private security to watch their backs, only an over-extended police force.
Eugene 04 35 05 12 I have been hit twice over the head by these so called gangsters the first time I spent two days in hospital the 2nd time was about 4 days in hospital
Script: Eugene Gordon started a neighbourhood watch 11 years ago in Cloetesville to claim back the streets for their children
04 05 40 09 it took us about 3 or 4 years to clear this area of elements. We got to that point where our children can go around the corner to the shops although safety is never guaranteed.
Script: It’s Friday night, and Eugene’s team are armed with little more than a radio, provided by the municipality. But he thinks it’s the justice system that’s failing them
Eugene 04 15 47 12 the criminals are repeated offenders they are either out on bail, out on parol, they are the guys doing it. So if we can’t stop them how are we going to stop the guys starting now, because they know crime pays. But we as normal citizens are the people that pay the actual price
Script: James has become a thorn in Mayor Gessie Van Deventer’s side, pressurising her to do more with money raised from private business, but she says it’s outside her mandate.
Upsound Gessie 02 21 06 11 Unfortunately we are not allowed City police, we are not a city like Cape Town can do that, I wish we could, if we were given a mandate to have a police force I would love that
Script: So private business formed the Winelands Safety Initiative, a section 21 company, with Andre Peltz, chair of the Ratepayers Association, as one of its board members.
Andre “Private security companies are there to secure private property, the public space is where the problem lies and that is where the police have such limited capabilities and we are trying to augment and supplement that in various ways
Script: One of which is a crack paramilitary security company, stationed in central Stellenbosch targeting ATM criminals and general crime. They can react quickly, and give the backup the police need. In just 3 months, crime is down by 50%. The other game-changer is the Licence Plate recognition software which alerts the network to suspect vehicles and people entering Stellenbosch
Andre 01 48 29 12 The crime intelligence operations of SAPS is very, very important and I think James makes a significant contribution to that network. I would be very careful straying outside that and you start doing policing and you are not registered and then you get into risky territory and that is my concern
TSU giving Chase-
01 00 56 05 it’s not me its people coming together, its synergies that are unlocked and it would not be possible without our brilliant SAPS members.
Script. James is bowing out. The ATM gangs are threatening him after he turned down a R40 000 bribe to look the other way.
“I have decided to retire
Script: But it’s hard habit to kick, after the thrill of over 2000 hours of chasing criminals

Tragically Jeffrey Zetler was stabbed to death in a botched robbery at his farm gate. Script: Six guys jumped Zetler as he opened the gate, stabbing him and then they dragged him to the office door, explains Zetler’s older brother Dennis Dennis “the alarm went off and then they punched him with a sharp object another 2 or 3 times because he had like 6 holes in his body before he left here so nobody could survive with all that bleeding Script: He collapsed before he could open the safe and they got away with nothing, says farm manager Jaco Vermeulen Jaco 07 40 18 14 We don’t know what to say we are speechless 07 39 50 18 it was a quiet Saturday afternoon and this was well planned …people watching our businesses’ Dennis 07 33 11 04 and you just think who is the next one that’s how I fear the whole time Script: Tourists love the relaxed atmosphere of this student town, filled with art galleries and boutiques, and that’s a magnet for ATM criminals. But they are difficult to catch and prosecute, because they make speedy getaways onto the Cape Flats Script: As the vice chair of the community policing forum, James has made it his business to bust the ATM gangs after hearing from guest house owner Annemien Kotze how often her clients were victims Annemein: 07 08 19 07 the guest were very upset when they arrived here it happened about once or twice a week and they just feel it spoiled their whole experience of the town and of Stellenbosch and their holiday to SA James driving 00 48 17 10 what you have is you will have your spotters standing somewhere in the street alerting the ATM robbers that there are tourists around and not a lot of policemen around Script: This is one of James’s informants. He has been working with the ATM gangs for the last 10 years. Eitenne” 11 06 48 17 I must listen to the accent of people talking… you must tell them hoe gaan dit and now you must listen to what they say back to you and if they say dit gan goed or goeden dagen then ..then I know what to do Link: 01 09 24 05 so underneath this car over here there is a square disk and this is a parking meter which is linked to the town’s system. What they will then do with an unsuspecting tourist is tell them that they need to pay for this parking meter at this ABSA ATM so when the tourist goes there this is where the charm and scam then kicks in ATM spotter 10 54 29 21 when you put your card inside the machine makes a click sound and the guy always has money in his right hand when the machine makes a click. He slides the card underneath the money and then he has this guy’s card in his hand now and now he tell the guy ok put in your pin 10 55 44 00 any way you move your hand he knows exactly which number you press… he tells you please you must wait the transaction is still in progress and while you wait he goes and he has your card already and he goes to the other machines and draw your money. R83 000 on one card and that is one card and sometimes they are standing there the whole day Script: The ATM gangs move swiftly, passing the stolen card between them so they’re almost impossible to catch. James had had enough, and was hell-bent on driving them out of town James 00 27 47 15 so what I started doing was I started following them and I started to disrupt them Mac “How? how did you disrupt them? That’s quite brave laugh James” you can take photos of them they don’t like that you can pull them over SAPS will come and they will profile them and search the car Script: Sometimes when he gives chase in his car they have an accident, or if they’re getting away, he uses his car as a battering ram James” I had a clear sight to see that there aren’t people around ….. and I just gave gas and I hit them ATM guy 11 04 07 11 for them he is like a demon to them because when they see him they run away …….when James see the cars and they don’t want to stop then he hit the cars when he is chasing them that’s what James do so they are very scared of James. Script: ATM crime is down dramatically. But the other major magnet for crime in this town are the 30 000 university students. Link: 05 57 05 21 So this is party central in Stellenbosch the students have come out to play the streets are lit and they having an amazing time but this is when they are most vulnerable because they have been drinking they are beyond caring TSU Doron Cozons 05 43 20 04 you have predators out there you have lots of people coming from different parts of Cape Town they see the naivety of these students. There are syndicates operating around here stealing lots of stuff from students Script: Last year, the abduction, rape and murder of student Hanna Cornelius, right in town, left the community reeling, but students still take chances despite the massive awareness campaigns. Emma Wieham says students are constantly preyed upon Emma 03 17 48 06. I know of a girl ...she was walking down Victoria which is the main road of campus, and they opened the car door and they grabbed her cellphone and she didn’t want to let go and they dragged her next to the car down the road. In that area there are a lot of cameras and people still have the audacity to try and get away with something like this Links 03 59 20 06 The unique thing about Stellenbosch University is that it is right in the heart of town and completely open to the public. The problem here is that anyone can walk right in and for students they become particularly vulnerable for criminals as their laptops their cellphones make for easy pickings Student 03 02 06 13 I was going to meet someone outside the res …not even two metres from the door he just started running at me. We still don’t know what his intensions were. He didn’t say anything he didn’t ask me for my phone. It was only afterwards that I realised I had been stabbed. It was on my left hand side close to my heart 10 cm deep and it eventually led to my lung collapsing and 4 days in ICU Script: Professor Stan du Plessis says that after this incident, The university improved the lighting and placed permanent guards at residences Prof Stan “It is never possible to say the precise reason crime is down is it because of our awareness campaign or of the technology that we use but we can say we have dramatically improved our system and we are happy to report the incidents of crime has declined Script: But across town in Cloetesville, they have other problems, drugs and gangs, and they don’t have the luxury of private security to watch their backs, only an over-extended police force. Eugene 04 35 05 12 I have been hit twice over the head by these so called gangsters the first time I spent two days in hospital the 2nd time was about 4 days in hospital Script: Eugene Gordon started a neighbourhood watch 11 years ago in Cloetesville to claim back the streets for their children 04 05 40 09 it took us about 3 or 4 years to clear this area of elements. We got to that point where our children can go around the corner to the shops although safety is never guaranteed. Script: It’s Friday night, and Eugene’s team are armed with little more than a radio, provided by the municipality. But he thinks it’s the justice system that’s failing them Eugene 04 15 47 12 the criminals are repeated offenders they are either out on bail, out on parol, they are the guys doing it. So if we can’t stop them how are we going to stop the guys starting now, because they know crime pays. But we as normal citizens are the people that pay the actual price Script: James has become a thorn in Mayor Gessie Van Deventer’s side, pressurising her to do more with money raised from private business, but she says it’s outside her mandate. Upsound Gessie 02 21 06 11 Unfortunately we are not allowed City police, we are not a city like Cape Town can do that, I wish we could, if we were given a mandate to have a police force I would love that Script: So private business formed the Winelands Safety Initiative, a section 21 company, with Andre Peltz, chair of the Ratepayers Association, as one of its board members. Andre “Private security companies are there to secure private property, the public space is where the problem lies and that is where the police have such limited capabilities and we are trying to augment and supplement that in various ways Script: One of which is a crack paramilitary security company, stationed in central Stellenbosch targeting ATM criminals and general crime. They can react quickly, and give the backup the police need. In just 3 months, crime is down by 50%. The other game-changer is the Licence Plate recognition software which alerts the network to suspect vehicles and people entering Stellenbosch Andre 01 48 29 12 The crime intelligence operations of SAPS is very, very important and I think James makes a significant contribution to that network. I would be very careful straying outside that and you start doing policing and you are not registered and then you get into risky territory and that is my concern TSU giving Chase- 01 00 56 05 it’s not me its people coming together, its synergies that are unlocked and it would not be possible without our brilliant SAPS members. Script. James is bowing out. The ATM gangs are threatening him after he turned down a R40 000 bribe to look the other way. “I have decided to retire Script: But it’s hard habit to kick, after the thrill of over 2000 hours of chasing criminals Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Stellenbosch under siege? metadata.Unique Selling Point: James Hayes is a successful businessman living in Stellenbosch. He grew up there, studied at the university and sees it as his home, but when he moved back there a few years ago he was horrified by the high level of crime and the municipalities apathetic approach towards protecting its residents. He could have sat back like most of us and just paid his subscriptions and attended the local ratepayers meetings. But as a former police reservist he is well versed with the law and how criminals operate. He recognizes the local police are over stretched and security companies have guards that are under paid and poorly trained. Angered by how tourists were being targeted by ATM gangs and the lack of effective policing James took it upon himself to drive them out of town by chasing them and driving into them. He was also angry by the lack of action against the gangs preying on hikers and students in the green belt so he put up a drone, tracked them down, and chased them with the help of local security company and caught 6 or the 7 heavily armed gang. James dedication and unconventional methods ruffle feathers. Nobody likes to be challenged by a private individual who is putting his body on the line to stop crime. He works closely with all the security networks and police and provides them with information from his well established network of informers. He is so disruptive to the gangs trade that they are trying to buy them off, or kill him.
metadata.Summary: Stellenbosch - the iconic university town with its oak-lined streets, cafes, boutiques and art galleries makes it a major tourist destination in the Western Cape. It’s surrounded by prestigious wine farms and home to some of the wealthiest people in the country, but on the outskirts are some of the poorest of the poor, in suburbs like Kayamandi and Cloetesville. The residents of Stellenbosch feel they are under siege, it has the 11th highest crime rate in the country, despite the relatively small population of 180 000 and over seven different security companies operating in town. It’s a story about how one small town, a microcosm of South Africa, is fighting back with private citizens challenging local municipalities to step up and protect them.
metadata.Further information: There are three levels of crime in Stellenbosch: in the wealthy suburbs it ranges from the usual house break-ins to violent house invasions. In town, the biggest crime is by ATM gangs which move into Stellenbosch from Khayelitsha, Guguletu and Sea Point. With eight ATM syndicates operating in the Western Cape, Stellenbosch makes for easy pickings with plenty of access routes in and out of town. The ATM gangs descend on Stellenbosch in several hired cars, using local car guards to call them when the tourists are in town, and ensure bank security is paid off. They only target tourists because they don’t have limits on their cards, have insurance and won’t bother to press charges because they won’t be around to appear in court. One morning they made off with R86 000 from just one card holder – they can make millions of rand every month. Once a card is snatched/swopped they pass it so rapidly from one person to the next that the police have given up trying to catch them. Then there are the students, who account for 1/3rd of crime victims in Stellenbosch. It’s an open campus and students drink in town and fall foul to petty crimes like cell-phones and laptops being snatched, to more extreme crime like kidnapping , rape and murder. First year student Hanna Cornelius was abducted, raped and murdered last April, attacked while sitting talking to a friend in her car in the early hours of the morning. The farms surrounding Stellenbosch are constantly under attack, the latest victim Jeffrey Zetler, a high profile member of the Stellenbosch community, well loved and respected by his workers. He was murdered in front of his staff on 23rd June as he was locking up. Zetler paid his staff in cash, a fact well known by local criminal networks. He had survived three previous robberies. The head of the Farmers’ Association, Piet Carinus, says most farmers don’t deal in cash anymore because they are followed home from the bank and have given up on expecting protection or help from SAPS. And then there is Cloetesville and Kayamandi which are ravaged by drugs and gang turf wars. Neighbourhood watch chair Eugene Gordon says that 47 people lost their lives last year in Cloetesville alone. James Hayes, a successful businessman who grew up in Stellenbosch, studied at the University and recently moved back with his family, was horrified by the high crime rate. Soon after he bought his home he discovered the previous owner was attacked by the infamous crowbar gang on several occasions, and in the last incident he had a gun held to his head. James immediately installed massive lights on top of his home and security cameras on his street. Having been a police reservist for many years, James decided to get actively involved in defending himself and his neighbourhood and made it his business to get to know all the security networks in town. Currently he is the Vice Chair of the Community Policing forum. James makes for an unusual resident. He spends most of his spare time tracking criminals, regularly patrolling the streets at night. He is on a radio network with several neighbourhood watches, security companies, and has a network of informers. He makes it his business to go out and confront crime as it’s happening. He prides himself in having a bullet proof vest and when his network of informers tells him the ATM gangs are in town he races off after them. The police have given up chasing them, so James has made it his mission - on several occasions when chasing the ATM gangs he has bashed into them using the bullbar on his Nissan, literally driving them out of town, to the extent that the ATM gangs are now scared of him and leave town if they are alerted to his presence. And like all other people that obstruct their business, the gangs are now offering him R40 000 a month to stay away. That’s not working, so now there are death threats directed at him and his network of informers. But his unconventional methods are having an impact, and ATM crime is right down from where it was over the festive season. James was tired of the attacks on hikers and runners at African Valley. When he approached the Municipality they refused to put up a sign warning people of gangs in the area saying it was bad for tourism. So James set up a sting. He put a drone up and was directed by radio to where the gang was spotted and chased them down with two local security bringing down 6 of the 7 criminals. He has the drone footage the pictures gang and the weapons. When he catches criminals he profiles them and shares the information with the police and security networks. James acknowledges that like all South African towns there are just not enough or sufficiently well-trained police officers. They are fighting heavily armed gangs, petty criminals, drug protection syndicates, and civilian protests for better service delivery. The Municipality doesn’t see fighting crime as its responsibility apart from protecting municipal property. Winelands Security Watch is a new initiative which is sponsored by several wealthy business people who took on the services of security company TSU. They are well-armed and are making an impact in the central zone of Stellenbosch. They have also installed a Licence Plate Recognition system and have begun profiling every ATM criminal, and crime figures are down over the last few months. But all this does is displace crime from well-defended suburbs to areas where the guards are underpaid and poorly trained, making them open to being paid off. We will go on patrol with the neighbourhood watch in Cloetsville- they have been on the beat for 11 years. With James his daily night patrols and TSU the new crack team in town and see the Licence plate tracking unit. We will also feature the students as they party it up and hear their side of the story. Interview the farmers and Zetlers widow. I already have an interview with one of the ATM gangs who tells us how its done.
